html:
Jumia is an online marketplace with its own delivery and payment services, founded in Lagos, Nigeria, in 2012. In April 2019 it became the first African tech start-up to list on the New York Stock Exchange.

It was set up with backing from the German start-up builder Rocket Internet, on the model of Amazon. Selling online in Africa meant solving problems from scratch: few street addresses, patchy roads, and buyers without bank cards. Jumia built its own logistics network and accepted cash on delivery, and later added its own payment service, JumiaPay. It spread to more than a dozen African countries.

The stock market listing made headlines as a milestone for African tech, then drew criticism. Some asked whether a company with head offices in Berlin and Dubai was really African, and the share price fell sharply after a short seller's report. Jumia has never been profitable and has since left several countries to cut costs.
sum: Jumia is an online marketplace with its own delivery and payment services, founded in Lagos, Nigeria, in 2012. In April 2019 it became the first African tech start-up to list on the New York Stock Exchange.
